author: adrianduta96
title: Motion Graphics Music Machine
prompt: Make a 20-second 16:9 motion graphics video that tells a little story with sound. For the first 12 seconds there is no sound at all: on a warm paper background, the words "make it catchy." type themselves out, then the letters fall apart and build a colorful music machine piece by piece: ramps, spinning gears, a row of blocks like piano keys and a big drum. It ends with a ball waiting at the top. At 12 seconds the ball drops and the machine comes alive. Every block it hits plays a note, the drum kicks, the gears tick in rhythm, and it all becomes a catchy 4-second beat. Then everything snaps into the words "ONE PROMPT" on a final hit, followed by silence. Use bold geometric shapes in ink black, cobalt blue and sunflower yellow, and make every sound match a movement you can see. Go all out and render the final MP4.
postText:
One prompt. Claude Opus 5.5 made this whole clip: the animation, the typography and the music.

And it didn't stop there.

Claude also edited the final video from my raw recording: the cuts, the captions, the layout and the sound mix. All I did was record myself, give Claude the raw video and write a normal prompt.

For the clip itself, there was no stock music and no sound effects library.
Claude wrote every sound and synced each one to a movement on screen.

It took about 30 minutes from prompt to finished clip.

A year ago this was a job for a motion designer, an animator, a sound designer and an editor. Now it's a first draft you can get by working with claude.

Here is the exact prompt I used for the clip:

"Make a 20-second 16:9 motion graphics video that tells a little story with sound. For the first 12 seconds there is no sound at all: on a warm paper background, the words "make it catchy." type themselves out, then the letters fall apart and build a colorful music machine piece by piece: ramps, spinning gears, a row of blocks like piano keys and a big drum. It ends with a ball waiting at the top. At 12 seconds the ball drops and the machine comes alive. Every block it hits plays a note, the drum kicks, the gears tick in rhythm, and it all becomes a catchy 4-second beat. Then everything snaps into the words "ONE PROMPT" on a final hit, followed by silence. Use bold geometric shapes in ink black, cobalt blue and sunflower yellow, and make every sound match a movement you can see. Go all out and render the final MP4."

What would you use this for in your work?

#ai #claude #motiondesign #generativeai #videoediting

Camera: locked and front-on for the whole film, like a drafting table. Objects turn; the camera never moves.
Empty border: nothing at rest within 150 px of the sides or 90 px of the top and bottom. Things travelling through may cross it.

Three inks. The same geometry is drawn in whichever ink is on screen:
- PAPER: a cream paper background (use my paper image if I give one, otherwise flat cream with fine drawn grain) with a 60 px blue grid at about 13% and every fifth line at 26%. Lines are pencil: resampled and pushed off true by slow sine waves whose phase changes 8 times a second, stroked twice (full width at 90%, half width at 40% with more wobble), with paper tooth knocked out of the strokes, then multiplied onto the paper. Fills are diagonal hatching drawn on one line at a time. Big type is hatching cut to the letter shapes, with a doubled outline.
- BLUEPRINT: flat blue with the same grid in white. Clean white lines 3 to 4 px, hidden edges dashed and thinner, fills are fine clean hatching.
- HOLOGRAM: black with the same grid in cyan. Cyan lines with a white core 30% of the line width. Fills are horizontal scan lines on an 8 px pitch whose thickness follows how lit the surface is. No blur halo anywhere: it reads as light through line density only.

Banned: particle bursts, glows, lens flares, camera shake, RGB split, crossfades, generic gradients, bouncy easing, holds longer than half a second, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 60 beats, 15 bars of 2 seconds. Something happens on every beat. Moves start 0.05 s before their beat so they land on it.

Scene changes: paper to blueprint by a shape that floods the frame with a hard edge; blueprint to hologram and hologram to paper by one horizontal scan line.

title: Three.js Castle Above Clouds Experience
prompt:
Build one self-contained, real-time Three.js PBR web experience titled: CASTLE ABOVE CLOUDS

Subtitle lockup: A DREAM IN THE SKY · REBUILT
Hero line, large, two weights: Above the
postText:
1、Paste it into YouWare, pick Claude Opus 5.5, send → https://www.youware.com/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=steal&utm_content=20261010-castle-above-clouds 

2、Full Prompt:
「Build one self-contained, real-time Three.js PBR web experience titled: CASTLE ABOVE CLOUDS

Subtitle lockup: A DREAM IN THE SKY · REBUILT
Hero line, large, two weights: Above the clouds, / there lives a castle.
Small supporting line under it: Drift slowly around eaves and towers, timber walkways and floating cottages. Moonlight skims the stone walls, and warm lamps come on in rooms where people live.
Top-right badge: REAL-TIME PBR SCENE
Bottom-right telemetry: Coordinates 32.7° N · 118.4° E / Moonlight · Breeze · Cloud layer 1,200 m
Vertical side credit: STYLIZED WEB THREE.JS
Bottom-left: zoom in / zoom out / reset / orbit icons.

This is not a still. It is a screen-recordable product shot of a live scene. Mouse orbit, scroll zoom, slow auto-orbit when idle. Hold 60fps. Pixel ratio capped at 2.

WORLD
Night sky, deep blue-black, not pure black. Large pale moon, soft clouds at several depths, a few small stars. Cloud layer sits around the islands, not below the whole world. Faint breeze moves clouds and tiny pennants.
A cluster of floating rock islands. Undersides are dark, chunky, slightly mossy rock with hanging roots and a few dangling lanterns. Tops are lived-on ground: grass patches, stone paths, wooden decks.

HERO ISLAND
One large central castle-town, white plaster walls, warm stone base, red conical tower roofs, small yellow flags on the peaks.
Readable architecture, not a blob:
- main keep with a tall red spire
- attached round tower with slit windows
- lower wing with a green roof and open balcony
- wooden external stairs and a wraparound deck
- string lights along railings
- dozens of individual warm windows, some brighter, some dim, a few flickering
- a small market stall / awning on the lower terrace
- chimney, gutters, shutters, flower boxes if cheap
Scale is toy-like but materials are serious. Close orbit must not fall apart.

SATELLITE ISLANDS
At least six smaller floating islets at different heights and distances:
- one with a red-roof cottage and a chimney
- one with a white house and a warm porch lamp
- one almost empty rock with a single lantern
- one with a tiny tower and a flag
- two mid-size hamlets linked visually to the castle by implied paths, not a rigid grid
Each has its own rock underside. They bob very slightly, out of phase. No identical clones.

LIGHTING AND MATERIALS
Real-time PBR, stylized, not Unreal photoreal and not flat toon.
- Moon as key, cool, soft shadows
- Window and lantern emissive as practicals, warm 2200–2700K, bloom only on lights
- Stone slightly rough, plaster matte, roof tiles with a soft specular, wood with grain
- Rock undersides darker and rougher than the town
- A little atmospheric fog so far islands desaturate
- No harsh studio three-point. The moon path and window glow are the picture.

CAMERA
Start three-quarter above the castle, moon behind the towers.
Then a slow orbit: drop to deck level so string lights and windows read, slide past a satellite cottage, rise again to a high aerial of the whole cluster, return.
User can interrupt with drag and scroll at any time. Ease, no jitter.

UI
Editorial, dark glass, low chrome. Do not cover the castle. Left copy stays readable over sky. Right telemetry stays small. Cursor is a normal pointer; hovering a building can brighten its windows a touch, nothing else.

DO NOT
- Make one island with a castle texture
- Use a skybox city
- Add characters, combat, inventory, or a loading fantasy novel
- Go full Ghibli flat color or full photogrammetry
- Fake the float with a static render

Taste: a rebuilt dream you can orbit. Someone should be able to screen-record any second and it still looks like the product shot.」

author: aichrislee
title: Build me a camera lens in interactive 3D, in one HTML file with Three.js.
prompt:
Build me a camera lens in interactive 3D, in one HTML file with Three.js.

Make it look real: a big black pro zoom lens with its glass front, the rubber focus and zoom rings, the red stripe and the white numbers, and inside it the parts you never get to see. author: 0xKarmi
title: Deterministic Frame-Based Video Rendering
prompt:
Picture a butterfly with no memory of its last wingbeat.
Ask it for frame 720 and you get frame 0, pixel for pixel.

720 frames. 12 seconds. 6 counters. All at 0.

Opus 5.5 can't hand over a video file, one builder says. He made that gap the method.

> STAGE - one fixed 1000x1080 canvas, fonts baked in
> RENDER - a windowless engine calls draw(f) once per frame number
> ENCODE - ffmpeg writes H.264, pixel aspect ratio declared
> CHECK - three passes after every build

By his account the model writes only the first, a drawing program. The other three get reused.

Each picture depends on its number alone: no clock, no timer, no dice that land differently each run.

So any frame renders the same every time. A fix is a small edit and a re-render.

The sample loop is 720 pictures in 12 seconds. A hand animator at 12 drawings a second would need 144.

The smoke test plays one loop unseen and counts six kinds of defect, from script errors to text on text.
Six yes/no gates before a human looks.

The seam check puts frame 0 against frame 720. One changed pixel means some motion isn't periodic.

He reports a last render of 1,820 frames with six zeros. At the sample's 60 fps that would be about half a minute.

Let one frame read a clock and the same number stops giving the same picture.

We drew the rule as an X-ray butterfly, its wingbeat computed from the frame number ↓

author: fleyta88
title: GSAP Timeline with Frame Checking
prompt: Build a GSAP timeline for UI cards with specific timing constraints: 280ms for cards, 220ms for title, 160ms for metadata, and a 60ms stagger between elements. Implement a verification loop where the animation is stepped through frame-by-frame using Playwright, screenshots are compared to detect overshoot or errors, and the code is patched until it passes the checks without rewriting everything.
postText:
i watched opus 5.5 get its own animation checked frame by frame. it got caught making an 8% mistake that most people would never notice

most ai motion demos end when something looks smooth. this one keeps going until the numbers actually match.

280ms for the cards. 220ms for the title. 160ms for metadata. a 60ms stagger between elements.

not a single "make it polished" instruction anywhere.

the interesting part is what happens after opus writes the animation.

instead of trusting the first render, the system breaks the entire sequence into frames and checks what actually moved.

the loop looks like this:

→ opus builds the gsap timeline from exact curves  
→ playwright steps through the animation frame by frame  
→ screenshots become one contact sheet  
→ the critique catches 8% overshoot  
→ opus patches the numbers without rewriting everything  
→ the checker runs again until it passes

think about what changed here.

the model isn't being asked whether something feels good. it's being asked exactly when an element started moving, where it stopped, and how far it traveled.

a 60ms difference can change the entire rhythm of an interface. one unnecessary bounce can make an otherwise clean animation feel cheap.

and the fix isn't another giant prompt telling opus to be more creative.

it's giving the model a way to prove what it built.

we've spent years teaching ai to write animation code. now we're finally giving it a clock and a way to check its own work.

the next time someone tells an ai to "make it smoother," i'd love to know which frame they actually want fixed.

Shape damping 0.72, settle time 0.35s.

Encode to H.264 at 60fps.

Use a ripple from the center at 1.5s and from the click point at 12.0s.

Roll word swaps vertically.

Start draw-on after blur-in.

Aim the cursor at where the target will be when it lands.

Keep cursor speed under 65 px/frame.

<start>
First show me the storyboard.

author: okazaky
title: Lyric MV 3D Engine Workflow
prompt:
Create a 50-second vertical music video using programmatic rendering (Three.js) instead of native video AI.
1. Generate song with Suno. Extract lyrics from embedded metadata.
2. Separate stems with Demucs (vocals, drums, bass, other).
3. Transcribe vocals with mlx_whisper. Align with official lyrics to create script where '1 lyric line = 1 scene'.
4. Write storyboard: define 'What to show in 3D', 'Camera', 'Main word' for each lyric line.
5. Have 4 parallel Opus sub-agents write scene programs.
6. Export 16-frame contact sheet for visual verification.
7. Render headless Chrome at 1080x1920, 60fps.
8. Normalize volume to -14 LUFS.
Style: Engraving-like lines, colors limited to Black, Bone, Orange.
postText:
50秒の縦長MVを、カメラも撮影素材も使わずに作りました。

曲はSunoで作り、映像はすべてプログラム（three.js）です。そのプログラムはClaude Codeに書かせました。

作り方と、使ったスキル・エンジンを全部公開します。

■ 何でできているか

この映像は「時刻を渡すと1枚の絵が決まる」プログラムです。28.11秒を渡せば、何度やっても同じ1枚が返ってきます。それを1秒に60回くり返して並べると、動画になります。

絵は写真ではなく線です。球も文字もビルも、細い縞を重ねて銅版画のように彫っています。色は黒・骨色・オレンジの3色だけにしています。

■ 土台にしたもの

海外の開発者 Giacomo Magnanini さんが公開している歌詞MVのエンジン「pdoom-video」（MITライセンス）です。これもClaude Codeとの会話で作られたものです。前作でこれを改造し、今回その作り方をClaude Codeのスキルにまとめました。

■ 手順（スキル lyric-mv-3d の中身）

1. Sunoで曲を作る。Sunoのmp3には歌詞が埋め込まれているので、そこから取り出す
2. Demucsで曲を4つに分ける（歌・ドラム・ベース・それ以外）
3. 歌だけをmlx_whisperで文字起こしし、公式の歌詞と1文字ずつ照合して「歌詞1行＝1場面」の台割を作る
4. 絵コンテを書く。歌詞1行ずつに「何を3Dで見せるか・カメラ・主役の言葉」を決める
5. 場面のプログラムを、Opusのサブエージェント4体に並列で書かせる
6. 16コマを並べた一覧画像を書き出し、AI自身に目で確かめさせる
7. 画面を出さないChromeで、1080×1920・60fpsに書き出す（3049コマで23〜38分）
8. 音量を -14 LUFS にそろえる

2と3は、スクリプト1本で自動です。

■ 6つの版を作りました

朝9時45分に頼んで、いまの版（v6）ができたのは18時でした。3Dの版だけで v1 から v6 まであります。その間の指摘と直し方です。

・最初の2案（平面に文字を出すだけの映像）は「そういうのじゃない」で却下。前作の3D版を見本に渡し、その作り方をスキルにした
・「もっと動きが欲しい」→全場面に動きを足したら「0:28までは前のほうがいい」。前半を戻し、後半だけ作り直した
・歌詞の「クロ」「コード」はClaudeとcodeのこと。画面では英語で出すようにした
・「音の変わり目（0:15と0:28）に映像の変わり目が欲しい」。拍ごとの音量の差から変わり目を探した
・「若干ずれてる」。拍の単位（0.42秒刻み）で測っていたのが原因で、50ミリ秒刻みで測り直した
・最後は、映像を流しながら声で解説した動画を撮って8点を指摘し、それをAIに文字起こしさせて直した

■ 一番効いた発見

0:28の「開く」瞬間です。最初はドラムが戻る28.54秒で切り替えていましたが、見ると遅れて見えました。楽器ごとに分けて測り直すと、上の音だけが0.4秒早い28.12秒に鳴っていました。耳が「開いた」と感じていたのはこちらでした。

歌詞も同じです。文字起こしのAIは、言葉の中の音を等間隔だと仮定して時刻をつけます。最初の「く」は1.58秒とされていましたが、実際に歌声が立ち上がるのは2.05秒でした。歌声の立ち上がりを探し、曲の8分音符の格子に並べ直すと、「く」と歌った瞬間に「く」が出るようになりました。

■ 私がやったこと

決まりを書いたのはAIです。私がしたのは、出来上がった映像を見て、どこがずれているかを言葉にして伝えることでした。

直した点は、そのたびにスキルの「好みの欄」へ書き足しています。次の曲では、同じ指摘をしなくて済みます。

■ 公開しているもの

https://github.com/okazaky/claude-skill-lyric-mv-3d

・skill/ … Claude Codeのスキル本体（手順・台割を作るスクリプト・絵コンテの雛形）
・engine/ … 改造したthree.jsのエンジン
・examples/yoru-code/ … この動画の絵コンテ・場面のコード・修正の記録

使った道具: Claude Code（Opus 5.5）／Suno／three.js／bun・Vite／Demucs／mlx_whisper／ffmpeg

title: Pixel Art Voiceover Film
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a voiceover or song with a spoken line (the audio file) and its transcript, 10-12 small objects that sum up my life, two silhouettes to light like a heat camera (a head in profile and a raised hand), and the 3 words I want to land hardest. If I skip any, use the defaults: vinyl, book, camera, cat, coin, game controller, cap, heart, money, plant, clapperboard, skateboard; free CC0 silhouettes from Openverse; action, intention, curiosity.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 20 second 4:3 film, 1440x1080 at 60fps, cut to the voice. Off-white paper, black, one red, one yellow, Geist for every word. Film grain on everything, a soft vignette, and a camera that never rests: a slow handheld float under everything plus a slow push inside every scene.
No scene cuts to the next: each handoff starts on the exact last frame of the scene before. The only hard cuts are the beat flips on the last word.
Every object is pixel art you draw yourself: a 16x16 grid per object, every cell a hand-placed colour, rendered as a 3D block (a darker extrusion down-right, a thin bevel on every cell) with a soft contact shadow.
The silhouettes are lit like a heat camera: the heat comes from how thick the body is at each point, so the nose, the hair and the fingertips run cooler, plus one hotspot and a slow moving noise, mapped through a black > red > orange > cream ramp. The edge stays razor sharp, with a soft glow outside it.
Motion rules: nothing pops in (eased glides of about 0.5s with a soft start), fast moves get real motion blur instead of ghost copies, and captions type with the voice behind a block cursor.
Banned: stock footage, AI video, 3D camera moves, particles, glitch.
</direction>

<structure>
Hang every scene on the transcript's word timings (measure them with faster-whisper word timestamps, one short chunk at a time):
1. The first word fills a yellow card. The card wipes off to the left and the question types underneath on two centred lines that glide to stay centred as they grow, the key word underlined in red as it's spoken.
2. The objects streak past in lanes above and below the words, a cyan four-point flare sweeps in, then the page burns away: black closes in from the edges onto the head, behind a hot red edge.
3. The head heats up on black while the answer types low on the left. A thin white orbit draws itself around the head, its far half passing behind it. On the last word, paper blooms out from inside the head with the objects in it, and the camera falls through: the head rushes past the lens until the paper is all we see.
4. The objects sit on a tilted ring seen in perspective (the front ones bigger and lower, drawn last), slowly turning, each one bobbing; the coin flips and lands with sparks.
5. On each of the 3 words, that object flies out of the ring to the left and grows, the page floods black from it, and the word types beside it (camera: a red shutter star; book: a red ribbon sweep; record: two white orbits and red notes). Then the flood drains back into the object as it flies home, and the camera dives closer into the ring. Put each hero object in the slot that is front-left when its word lands.
6. The ring pulls in a touch, bursts outward, every object turns to ink, and ink blots grow and swallow the page.
7. The hand rises into frame, hot, with the line split either side of it. The heart drops into its palm, then lifts to the centre at the size the next scene holds it.
8. The last word, one letter per beat, the background flipping paper / black / red, the heart holding its place across the cut, the centre object morphing pixel by pixel into the next one.
9. Thin brush strokes sweep through, the letters drift apart and float, then settle back into the word with the heart above it. The camera keeps pushing through the hold.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. Bake each pixel sprite once to an offscreen canvas (the extrusion layers, then the face), then draw it scaled and rotated.
3. The heat: precompute each silhouette's base heat once (a distance transform of the mask, held at the edge value outside it so nothing dark bleeds in when it is upscaled). Every frame, add the hotspot and two octaves of value noise at quarter resolution, map it through a 256-step lookup, upscale it, and cut it with the full-resolution mask.
4. The fall through the head: draw the ring scene into an offscreen layer, mask it with the head scaled up about a point inside the skull, and grow that scale on a cubed curve until the head covers the frame. The ring inside zooms less than the head does, so it reads as depth.
5. The pixel morph: pair every cell of object A with a cell of object B and glide each one's position and colour, with a small random delay per cell.
6. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 8 motion-blur subframes, then lay the original audio back on with ffmpeg.
</build>

<gotchas>
A mask PNG with no alpha channel fills the whole box with heat, so put the silhouette in the alpha. A limb cut by the photo's border shows as a straight edge, so extend the mask past the frame. A handoff only reads as smooth when the last frame of one scene is the first frame of the next: draw the outgoing scene under the transition, and give scenes that show the same ring one shared zoom function. A flood that's still retreating when the next scene starts reads as a hard cut, so let it finish first. A fast ease-out flood reads as a jump; use a soft start.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, measure the word timings, then show me 8 stills before you render.
</start>

author: MrKindey
title: Self-Building 3D House Animation
prompt:
No plugins, no app, just a single HTML file running Three.js on WebGPU.

It's an interactive 3D house that builds itself in five stages: Foundation → Skeleton → Systems → Envelope → Finished. Every part has its own window on the timeline, so you can scrub through the construction like a video.

What's inside:
→ X-ray mode that makes the structure transparent and shows the water, power, sewage and airflow routes, with filters for each system
→ Explode, to pull the layers apart
→ Cut, a section plane that slices through the building
→ Dusk, a lighting switch to see it at night
→ Instanced vegetation, so a dozen olive trees cost almost nothing to render
→ Callouts and preset cameras for each stage

The subject is a traditional hillside villa, but the format works for any building. A developer could show a buyer exactly what's behind the walls before a single wall exists.

postText:
プロンプト

あなたは一流のモーションデザイナー兼クリエイティブエンジニアです。
添付の曲を紹介する、SNS投稿用のトラックカード動画を作ってください。

## 成果物
- 1920×1080（16:9）・60fps・約15秒のMP4（音あり、AAC 192kbps、−14 LUFS）
- 同じ映像をブラウザで再生できる単一のHTMLファイル（フォントとデータを埋め込み、外部ファイルなしで動くこと）
- 作業フォルダ：{保存先フォルダ}

## 曲の情報（画面に出す文字）
- 曲名：{SUBTONE CONVERSATIONS} ／ 日本語：{サブトーン・カンバセーションズ}
- 説明文（2行）：{1行目} ／ {2行目}
- 主な音（タグ3つ）：{タグ1}、{タグ2}、{タグ3}
- 拍子：{4/4}（BPMとキーは音声から解析して入れる）
- アーティスト表記：{@TKZ_AIART／表示しない}

## 見た目（ジャズのレコードプレーヤー風カード）
- 背景：深い青の放射グラデーション＋うっすらフィルムグレイン。アクセント色は水色（#45B8F2 前後）
- 上部：画面の幅いっぱいに、等幅フォントで「JAZZ, NOW.  ON VINYL」、右端に曲中の再生位置（例 2:27 / 3:14）、その下に細い進捗バー
- 左半分：レコードプレーヤー（画面の高さの約70%の大きさ、縦方向の中央。画像素材を使わず、すべてcanvasで描く）
  - 角丸の本体、プラッター外周の回転するストロボドット、溝のあるレコード、静止した光の反射、
    曲名入りの回転するレーベル、トーンアーム（カウンターウェイト・ヘッドシェル付き）、つまみ2つ、電源ランプ
  - プレーヤーの下に小さく「LP · 33 1/3 RPM」
- 右半分（上から順に）：
  - 「TRACK 01」（アクセント色の等幅フォント）
  - 大きな曲名（右半分の幅にフィット、入らなければ2行に折る）
  - 日本語曲名（アクセント色）
  - 区切り線（アクセント色）
  - 拍子・BPM・キーを1行で（例 4/4   BPM 114   A MAJOR）
  - 説明文2行
  - 「主な音」の見出しと、タグ3つを横に並べる（角丸の枠）
  - 一番下に、実際の音から作ったスペクトルの縦棒（32本）
- 書体：曲名と日本語は Noto Sans JP（400/700/900）、ラベル類は IBM Plex Mono。日本語フォントは使う文字だけをGoogle Fontsの text= で切り出して埋め込む

## 音の切り出し（最重要）
1. librosaで曲を解析し、BPM・キー・小節の頭の位置を出す（BPMは onset の周期をくし形フィルタで精密に合わせる）
2. 小節ごとの音量と変化量を一覧にして、「静かな1小節 → バンドが一斉に入る」箇所を探す（曲中で一番盛り上がる区間の入口）
3. その静かな1小節の頭から、約15秒に一番近い小節数（114BPMなら7小節＝14.73秒）を切り出す
4. 静かな1小節はローパスでこもらせ、盛り上がりの頭から全帯域で鳴らす。最後の0.5秒はフェードアウト

## 動き（すべて切り出した音のタイミングに合わせる）
- 0秒：完成したカードがそのまま見える状態にする（このフレームがサムネイルになる）。アームは外側に置いた状態
- 0.3秒〜：アームが持ち上がり、レコードの上へ旋回。レコードは33⅓回転まで回り始める
- アームはゆっくり下り、盛り上がりの1拍目（＝2小節目の頭）にちょうど針が着地する。区切り線はこの1小節で伸びきる
- 着地の瞬間：電源ランプ点灯、カード全体が一瞬だけ少しふくらむ、背景が光る、曲名に光が一度走る
- 再生中：スペクトルは実際の音から（1フレームごとにFFTを取り、立ち上がりは速く、減衰はゆっくり）、背景の明るさは音量に連動、BPMの数字が拍で小さく跳ねる、針はゆっくり内側へ進む
- 最後：音のフェードアウトに合わせてアームが持ち上がる

## 技術的な条件
- 描画は seek(t) という「時刻tだけで決まる関数」にする。CSSのアニメーションや setInterval は使わない
- 動きはばねの閉形式（減衰振動の式）で計算する。モーションブラーは1フレームを4つのサブフレームで描いて平均する
- 経過時間の文字とグレインは、ブラーをかけずに1フレーム1回だけ描く
- 書き出しは Playwright（Chromium）で1フレームずつ PNG を取り出し、ffmpeg で H.264 にエンコードして音声と合わせる
- 注意：トーンアームの針の軌跡は、同じ半径の円と2回交わる。外側から内側へ探して「最初に交わる角度」を使うこと（逆を取ると針がレコードを横切る）

## 進め方
1. 先に音を解析して、切り出す区間とその理由（小節ごとの音量の表）を見せる
2. 本番の前に、主要な瞬間（0秒、アーム旋回中、着地直前、着地、中盤、終わり）の静止画を書き出して確認し、文字の詰まり・はみ出し・アームの位置を直してから全体を書き出す
3. 完成したら、MP4の長さ・フレーム数・音声が入っていることを確認して報告する

title: 15 Styles of Code-Generated Videos for Claude Opus 5.5
prompt:
做一支 10 秒彩色皮影戏，讲【曹冲称象】。剪影布局，暖光透背，关节式偶戏。依次出现秤盘、铜碗、石头，先平衡，再把石头分批称、加起来。字幕卡点出现。用代码渲染，导出可播放视频。

author: tanabe_fragm
title: Tile Mosaic Ad Video Prompt for Claude Opus 5.5
prompt:
添付の画像を「最後の画面」にして、全部タイルでできた30秒の広告動画（音つき・mp4）を作ってください。
ブラウザ（Three.js）で組み、Chromeで全コマを書き出し、ffmpegでmp4にします。

# ゴール
- 見る人は25秒、タイルの制作動画だと思って見る。最後の数秒で、添付画像（広告）だったと気づく
- 最後の画面は添付画像とほぼ同じ。文字が読める。画面いっぱいがタイル（床は見せない）

# 仕様
- 1920×1080、30fps、30秒。HTML1ファイル（Three.js。npmで入れてesbuildで1ファイルに固める）
- 時刻 t を渡すと、同じ t なら必ず同じ絵になる作りにする（seek(t)）
- タイルは1枚ずつ別のインスタンス。16:9の格子で約19万枚（576×324）
- 位置・向き・厚み・面取り・色を1枚ずつ変える。目地（隙間）は空き。線は引かない
- 添付画像は、タイルの色を取るためだけに使う（テクスチャとして貼らない）
- 素材は約12種（釉薬セラミック、スレート、真珠貝、白磁、テラコッタ、ガラスなど）。色の明るさと彩度で割り当てる
- 光は、左上の硬い太陽1つ。床は漆喰。奥に赤い大工のチョーク線がピンぼけで入る
- 被写界深度（円形ボケ）を後処理で自作する。しぼりは最初大きく、最後は小さく

# 流れ（秒）
0〜3　 床に暗いタイルが1枚。カメラは床すれすれ
3〜10　[組み始める場所]から、タイルが渦を巻いて落ちる。最初の1枚→周りの順に増える
10〜21 一気に外へ広がる。カメラが引いて[見せたい絵]が見えてくる
21〜24 全体が見える。文字になる場所は、周りと同じ淡い色のまま
24〜26 文字・ロゴ・ボタンのタイルが、左から順にパタパタ裏返って現れる
26〜30 真上からの構図で止まる。カーソルが[ボタンの文言]をクリックし、ボタンのタイルが少し沈む

# ハマりどころ（必ず守る）
- 文字になるタイルは、最初は周りの背景色で組む。背景色は、外側から内側へ塗り広げて決める。文字のふち（白ぶち）も一緒に裏返す。守らないと、途中で文字の形が見えてしまう
- 真上のカメラは、位置を真上ぴったりにしない（向きが90°回る）。止める所は、動きの勢いをゼロにする（補間のはみ出しで反転する）
- 最後の画面は、元画像と並べて色を比べ、露出・彩度・色味を合わせる
- 文字が小さくて読めないときは、タイル数を増やす
- 下地の暗い面は、タイルが着地したマスだけに出す

# 音
- ElevenLabsの効果音で、タイルを置く音・裏返す音・マウスのクリックを作る（各0.5秒）。作る前に、クレジットの消費を知らせる
- タイルの着地・裏返しの時刻に合わせて並べて重ねる。カメラが遠いほど小さく、数が増えたら雨のようにまとめる
- 24〜26秒のパタパタを、いちばん目立たせる。音量は -16 LUFS

# 進め方
1. 先に脚本（秒ごとの情景）を日本語で出し、OKをもらってから作る
2. 途中のコマ（最初のタイル／組み始め／引き／全景／文字が出る瞬間／最後）を自分で見て直す
3. 書き出しは Chrome（puppeteer-core）で seek(t) を30fpsぶん呼び、png を ffmpeg に流す
4. 納品は mp4（高画質と共有用）と、確認した画像

# 入力
- エンドフレーム: [添付]
- 組み始める場所: [例：人物の目]
- 引いたときに見せたい絵: [例：笑顔の女性]
- ボタンの文言: [例：無料体験はこちら]
postText:

prompt:

No images. Do not ask me any questions. Just build it.

author: rossaxbt
title: Product Promo Motion
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: one question a user asks my product and its one-line answer, two album covers, a royalty-free song around 110 BPM with a quiet intro and a hard drop (Mixkit, free for commercial use), and my logo for the ending. If I skip anything, use these defaults: "is this all code?" / "yes. every frame.", two atmospheric photos, and Mixkit "Head Bang".
</inputs>

<direction>
A 22-second square loop, 1440x1440 at 60fps. 2D only, one continuous take. Nothing cuts: each scene grows from the one before it, and every gesture carries the camera into the next space. Each morph takes 0.8s on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1). The camera zoom follows the same curve, making the shape changes feel almost invisible. Content dissolves during the second half of each glide. One gesture per scene.

Look: a warm light stage (#f3f3f0 to #e3e3de), black UI, and a dark app world (#121212) tinted by the current album cover. Use one green accent (#1ed760), Geist for UI, the real macOS pointer, and soft layered shadows that grow as shapes lift.

Banned: hard cuts, bouncy springs, particles, glows, zooming in and immediately back out, holds longer than 1s, anything that feels like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
Follow the song's beats. The press lands on the drop.

Generate: the cursor clicks. The pill glides into a spinner, then becomes a check.

Chat: the check splits into three typing dots with goo. The left dot flies up, becomes the question bubble and types the question. The right dot flies down into the reply. Both bubbles shrink back into dots as they glide toward the center and merge with the middle dot.

Play: the middle dot bends into a play triangle, one point at a time. The cursor presses it on the drop. A white button appears under the click as the dark app floods the frame around it, leaving the white shape as the play button. The camera pulls back to reveal the full now-playing screen: large cover, title, heart (liked, filling green), progress bar, controls and volume.

Swipe: the cursor drags the cover sideways. The next track slides in, and the app changes its tint to match the new cover.

Drag: the camera glides toward the volume slider. The cursor pulls it to max and keeps going. The bar rubber-bands, dragging the camera sideways out of the app and onto a dark dotted canvas while the camera follows the knob.

Chart: the line lands and curves upward into a green chart as the number counts up. The volume knob becomes the chart's final point.

Dive: the cursor clicks that point. The camera dives into it until the light stage fills the frame.

Ending: an "Ask [my product]" button grows from the light, narrows into a line, then fans out into my logo (default: the Claude spark, with six copies rotating into twelve rays in Claude orange). Hold for 2s.

author: RashadMirza404
title: Optogenetics Animation Explainer
prompt: Create a self-contained, aesthetically pleasing, breathtaking animation of optogenetics: how a light-sensing protein from green algae became a light switch for brain cells. Use JavaScript on a single canvas, all in one HTML file. Be detailed and scientifically accurate.
postText:
Prompt: Create a self-contained, aesthetically pleasing, breathtaking animation of optogenetics: how a light-sensing protein from green algae became a light switch for brain cells. Use JavaScript on a single canvas, all in one HTML file. Be detailed and scientifically accurate. It should evoke awe.

Structure it as one continuous journey through scales, in chapters, with a short caption at each stop explaining the science in plain language:

1. The alga. A single Chlamydomonas reinhardtii cell (about 10 µm) swimming toward sunlight, beating its two flagella. Show the cup-shaped chloroplast and the orange eyespot that senses light.

2. The eyespot. Zoom into the eyespot membrane and show channelrhodopsin proteins embedded in it.

3. The molecule. Zoom into one channelrhodopsin-2: seven transmembrane helices with a retinal chromophore inside. When a blue photon (~470 nm) arrives, the retinal flips from all-trans to 13-cis, the channel opens within about a millisecond, and positive ions (Na+, H+, Ca2+) pour through. Then it closes again.

4. The transfer. A modified virus (AAV) carries the channelrhodopsin gene into a chosen neuron. The neuron reads the gene, builds the protein, and places it in its outer membrane.

5. The switch. A thin optical fiber delivers pulses of blue light. Each pulse depolarizes the membrane and fires an action potential that travels down the axon, precisely timed to the light. Also show the opposite switch: a yellow-light-driven chloride pump (halorhodopsin) that silences the neuron.

6. The circuit. Zoom out to a network of neurons. Light drives one type of inhibitory neuron and produces gamma rhythms at around 40 Hz, visualized as synchronized waves (Cardin et al., 2009).

7. The brain. Zoom out to a whole mouse brain to suggest the scale: humans have about 86 billion neurons, and optogenetics lets researchers choose which cells to switch, and when, to the millisecond. Briefly show two results from the article: well-timed light lengthening hippocampal sharp-wave ripples to improve memory (2019), and a closed-loop system that detects a seizure and stops it with light (2013).

8. The eye. End with the human retina: in 2021, a man with retinitis pigmentosa partly regained sight after surviving retinal cells were made light-sensitive, using goggles that project amber light. Close on the thought that it all began with curiosity about how a tiny green cell finds the light.

Style: a dark, cinematic palette where the light itself is the hero, glowing blue and amber against deep greens and blacks. Use elegant serif typography with minimal on-screen text. Add smooth easing between chapters, a scale indicator, play/pause and restart buttons, and scroll or drag to move through it manually. It should be responsive down to mobile and respect reduced-motion settings.

Accuracy matters more than spectacle. Keep the colours, sizes, timings, and molecular details true to the real biology. Do not suggest that optogenetics can read or write thoughts, and make clear it is still mainly a research tool.

title: Product Launch Motion Film
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a one-word product name for the wordmark, one accent color, and a royalty-free track around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Product-launch UI motion in one continuous take. One shape tells the whole story: a prompt bar becomes a button, the button becomes a progress ring, the ring becomes a preview window, the window fills the screen, then shrinks into a toast and back into the prompt bar. No cuts, no fades between scenes: objects transform. A cursor triggers every change with real clicks. Warm off-white canvas, black UI, one accent color, Inter for UI and the wordmark. Springs everywhere with only a slight overshoot. Zoom the camera so each moment fills the square.
Banned: crossfades, gradients on UI, particles, glows, bouncy easing, dead beats, anything that feels like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 24 beats, something happens on every beat.
Type the request into the prompt bar → click send → the bar collapses into a black circle → a progress ring fills in four steps while four chips spring out (concept, storyboard, motion, sound) → the chips fly into a timeline and the circle becomes a preview window → a playhead sweeps the clips → inside the preview an orbit draws itself, a planet starts moving and the wordmark rises letter by letter from a mask line → the preview fills the screen → the letters drop away, the planet flies into a toast and becomes its checkmark → "Rendered in code · 60 fps" → the toast turns back into an empty prompt bar. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file with a 1440x1440 canvas. Draw everything inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form spring step responses. When a value changes target several times, add one spring per change so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The main shape is one rounded rect whose width, height, radius, position and color are each a chain of springs.
4. Typing is derived from time: characters shown = floor(progress × length), with a caret that blinks only when idle.
5. Find the beat grid of the track, start on a downbeat and place every click, pop and chime on its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright at 60 fps, then encode H.264 CRF 16 and loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render one still per beat first. Fix anything cramped, off-grid or hard to read before the full render.
</build>

<gotchas>
Text inside a morphing shape needs its own clip and separate enter/exit timing. Text swaps need their own fade so they never overlap. The cursor must end at the exact position it started, or the loop will stutter.
</gotchas>

author: ivanainai
title: Iron Man Helmet Three.js Animation
prompt:
Create a visually stunning, silent 3D browser animation of Iron Man’s classic red-and-gold helmet, presented as a premium cinematic studio object.

Deliver a complete runnable HTML experience using Three.js.

COMPOSITION

One helmet only, floating in the center of the
postText:
Prompt: Create a visually stunning, silent 3D browser animation of Iron Man’s classic red-and-gold helmet, presented as a premium cinematic studio object.

Deliver a complete runnable HTML experience using Three.js.

COMPOSITION

One helmet only, floating in the center of the frame.

Show the entire helmet, including its lower jaw and short armored neck opening. No shoulders, body, pedestal, or surrounding objects.

Make it large: approximately 70% of the viewport height, with enough space that it never clips during rotation.

Use a nearly black midnight-blue background, #070B14, with a very subtle studio gradient.

The finished helmet must be visible immediately. No introduction, loading sequence, titles, captions, logos, or interface over the scene.

THE HELMET

Make it immediately recognizable as Iron Man’s classic movie helmet.

Prioritize the correct silhouette and sculpted construction:
- A deep metallic crimson outer shell.
- A brushed gold faceplate with a strong angular brow.
- Narrow, sharply defined ice-white illuminated eyes.
- Sculpted cheek planes, a shaped nose bridge, and an angular armored jaw.
- A curved red crown, detailed temple panels, and a convincing rear shell.
- Fine recessed panel seams and small mechanical details.

Build real three-dimensional geometry with depth and thickness.

The front, sides, and back must all be intentionally modeled. The helmet must remain convincing through a complete rotation.

Create custom shaped surfaces and bevels where needed. Do not approximate the face with a collection of obvious boxes, spheres, or flat rectangular plates.

MATERIALS AND LIGHTING

Make the red shell look like polished automotive metal, with restrained micro-scratches and rich reflections.

Make the gold faceplate look like brushed metal, with subtle roughness variation.

Use broad studio lighting:
- A warm softbox from the upper left.
- A cooler, softer fill from the right.
- A narrow rim light that reveals the silhouette.

Create an environment that gives the metal readable reflections. Keep highlights controlled so the red and gold remain visible.

The eyes should emit a restrained white-blue glow. Preserve their sharp shape; avoid excessive bloom.

MOVEMENT

Keep the camera fixed at eye level with a subtle view from above.

Begin with the helmet facing forward.

Rotate the entire helmet smoothly around its vertical axis, completing exactly one full turn every 20 seconds.

Use constant rotation speed. No camera orbit, zoom, bobbing, wobbling, cuts, or extra animation.

The loop must be seamless.

IMPLEMENTATION

Construct the helmet procedurally in code. Do not download an existing helmet model or substitute a photograph, video, or flat image.

Use proper depth, lighting, shadows, antialiasing, and physically based materials.

Keep the composition responsive and consistent across viewport sizes.

Place a small replay control outside the scene, hidden unless the pointer moves.

Return the complete working implementation.

author: nilou_salehi
title: Across Product Demo Video
prompt: Take a look at our documentation and the product ux and generate a marketing video which narrates how our product works
postText:
We've been putting off creating demo videos of our product, because the team has been so busy building, talking to customers and generally just getting things done....

I know I know, marketing is and should be a priority but sometimes it just doesn't feel like you have enough hours in the day...

Anyway that being said wanted to share something here that's still rough (and yes, the AI voice is a bit much).

Our team gave Claude Opus 5.5, in Claude Code with ultracode on, one prompt:

- Take a look at our documentation and the product ux and generate a marketing video which narrates how our product works

.... and just like that we had the perfect video....

Okay not really but about 45 minutes later it did come back with a narrated, captioned first cut running in the browser, built on an animation we already had.

Three more rounds of my feedback got it to the video below. About 11 hours end to end, much of it unattended while review agents went over the video's own frames and it re-rendered. (as an aside there was no ffmpeg on my Mac, so it wrote its own renderer).

It shows how Across works, using an invoice example.

By no means the finished video, and it won't be the one that goes on our website but even building with these systems day to day I'm surprised by how capable they've become!

author: rossaxbt
title: Motion Design System
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a short label for the opening toggle, one hero word, a percentage for the graph, the text for the final card, one accent color, and a track with a clear beat.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 2D motion design film in 16:9. Use a warm off-white canvas, near-black backgrounds, bold typography and one vivid orange accent. The orange dot connects every scene: it starts in the UI, becomes the dot over a letter, traces a spring graph, grows into a shape and returns on the end card. A cursor makes the opening click feel real. Keep the motion sharp and controlled, with small spring overshoots and no dead time.
Banned: stock footage, gradients, glows, particle bursts, random transitions and motion that isn't connected to an element already on screen.
</direction>

<structure>
Around 15 seconds, with a visual change on every major beat.
Open: a cursor clicks the orange toggle beside "Reduce Motion". The letters bend and move into place until only "Motion" remains, with the orange dot above the "i".
Spring: the dot jumps away from the word and lands on a graph. Its path draws a spring response, overshoots the target and settles beside a "+22%" callout.
Shape: the dot shoots across a line, grows into an orange circle and fills the frame. A black rounded square rotates inside it, then stretches into a pill. The scene contracts to a single orange dot on black.
Type: words like "SPRINGS", "EASING", "KINETIC TYPE", "3D" and "SOUND" orbit the dot. The circle of type opens out into a field of tiny dots.
Reveal: the halftone field expands and flips to black, revealing the final card: "Opus 5.5", "Motion designer." and "0 keyframes".
Return: the orange dot moves back through the halftone, graph and toggle. Match the final frame to the first so the video loops cleanly.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, 1920x1080 at 60fps. Compute every visual from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form springs for the toggle, bouncing dot and graph. Draw the graph from the same spring function that moves the dot.
3. Animate letters individually for the "Reduce Motion" to "Motion" transformation. Keep the orange dot attached to the "i" until it begins its jump.
4. Make the orange circle, rotating square and pill different states of the same shape. Preserve its position and motion through each transformation.
5. Place the orbiting words along a circular path, then move their letters outward to hand the frame over to the halftone grid.
6. Draw the halftone as a grid of dots whose sizes respond to the orange dot. Let it grow past the frame edges before revealing the end card.
7. Sync the click, dot landing, graph peak, shape changes and final title to measured beats.

author: Pluvio9yte
title: Particle Effect Video Workflow
prompt:
公开我的制作方案，发给Opus5.5就能用

  1. 选素材

  三个标准，直接决定成败：

  - 主体完整：人物或物体全身入画。细节会在加工中丢失，观众靠轮廓认东西，特写会变成一团。
  - 背景干净：纯色、雪地、天空都行，主体和背景容易分开。
  - 有明确的动作瞬间：打击、起跳、落地、转身。这些是后面做特效的支点。

  来源可以是自己拍的、视频模型生成的，或有授权的现成片段。

  2. 拆素材

  从每一帧提取三类信息：

  - 颜色：原画面。
  - 远近：每个位置离镜头多远，用现成的深度估计模型算。
  - 主体范围：哪里是主体、哪里是背景。

  另外找出镜头切换发生在哪些时刻。这一步的要点是保持稳定：远近和主体范围要在同一个镜头内统一处理，否则播放起来会抖。

  3. 定"粒子"和"样式"

  先决定用什么东西来重建画面：圆点、方块、文字、线条都可以。

  然后设计几种样式。每种样式其实只是三条规则的不同组合：

  - 放在哪：整个画面都放，还是只放在主体上。
  - 多大：统一大小，还是跟着明暗、远近变化。
  - 什么颜色：用原画的颜色，还是统一用一两种颜色。

  再加一个开关：是平铺在一个面上，还是按远近推进三维空间。推进去之后镜头才能环绕。

  准备四到六种差异明显的样式就够用。粒子的疏密需要自己看着调：太大认不出内容，太小又和原片没区别。

  4. 找节奏

  - 定速度：选定音乐的速度，把时间切成等长的小格。让一格正好是整数帧，后面所有切换都好对齐。
  - 找动作瞬间：结合"声音突然变响"和"画面突然变动"两个信号，找出素材里的打击点。
  - 准备音乐：可以用现成的曲子并分析出它的拍子，也可以按定好的速度合成一段，并在打击点上加重音。

  5. 编排

  做一张时间表，写明每一格用哪种样式、什么配色、镜头在哪。这张表单独存放，以后调节奏只改它。

  编排的四条原则：

  - 开头交代变化：先给原画面，再过渡到粒子，让观众看懂发生了什么。
  - 快慢交替：一直快会麻木，中间要有一段明显慢下来的部分。
  - 配色要撞：相邻两格的颜色和样式反差越大，切换越有力。
  - 结尾要有收束：比如粒子越来越大直到变成色块，或者回到原画面。

  6. 关键时刻的反馈

  在打击点上叠加短促的反应，按轻重分级：

  - 每一次都有的轻反馈：粒子变形一下、镜头顶一下。
  - 较重时才有的中反馈：一部分粒子朝镜头弹开。
  - 最重的一两次才用的大反馈：时间静止，镜头环绕。

  原则是弱而短。只动一部分粒子，几帧内结束，否则画面炸成一片，观众就看不清主体在做什么了。

  贯穿全程的工作方法

  - 先小样后全片：每做完一个环节，先渲染几帧看效果，确认了再往下。全片只在最后渲染。
  - 拿不准的参数一次出一排：比如疏密，让 AI 同时出五六个档位并排放，你来挑。
  - 改哪里渲哪里：调整某一段时只重新渲染那一段。
  - 让 AI 自己看图：每一步都要求它把渲染结果打开看一遍再汇报。
  - 所有随机都固定：保证同样的设置每次渲染结果一致，否则没法逐步修改。

prompt:
Create a kinetic mathematical proof titled “THERE IS NO LAST PRIME.”
Stage Euclid’s argument as a beautiful mechanical inspection system. Typography becomes engraved number wheels, multiplication belts, and remainder indicators.
The mechanism must demonstrate the proof rather than decorate a narrated explanation.
DELIVERABLE
One self-contained HTML file.
1080×1080.
20.00-second loop.
Deterministic 60fps rendering.
Use SVG and/or Canvas.
No external runtime assets.

Porcelain # F0EEE6.
Graphite #222522.
Industrial green # 416B53.
Warning orange # E78636.
TYPE
Tabular monospace for all calculations.
Heavy geometric grotesque for declarations.
Small technical serif for the final logical statement.
Use disciplined spacing and large, readable numerals.
LOCKED COPY
SUPPOSE THE LIST ENDS.
MULTIPLY EVERY PRIME ON IT.
ADD ONE.
EVERY LISTED PRIME LEAVES REMAINDER 1.
A PRIME FACTOR IS MISSING.
THERE IS NO LAST PRIME.
CENTRAL EXAMPLE
Assumed list:
2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13
Product:
30030
Product plus one:
30031
Factorization:
30031 = 59 × 509
Both factors are absent from the assumed list.
IMPORTANT LOGIC
Do not claim that multiplying primes and adding one always produces a prime.
The constructed number may be composite.
Its prime factors cannot be any prime on the assumed complete list.
The numerical example illustrates the general contradiction.
STORYBOARD
0.00–3.00
SUPPOSE THE LIST ENDS.
Six engraved prime wheels lock into a finite inspection rack.
A physical end-stop closes after 13.
The end-stop makes the claim of completeness visible.
3.00–6.50
MULTIPLY EVERY PRIME ON IT.
A belt couples all six wheels.
Show a readable multiplication expression:
2 × 3 × 5 × 7 × 11 × 13 = 30030.
Use rolling numerals only during movement; settle the final value sharply.
6.50–8.50
ADD ONE.
A single orange unit enters the mechanism.
It advances the output from 30030 to 30031.
Make this one-unit change the decisive visual event.
8.50–12.50
EVERY LISTED PRIME LEAVES REMAINDER 1.
The output passes through six division gates.
Each gate is labelled with its prime.
Each produces the same visible remainder: 1.
Arrange the six completed results so the audience can compare them simultaneously.
12.50–15.50
The output opens as a labelled mechanical casing.
Inside, reveal:
59 × 509.
These factors cannot fit into the supposedly complete rack.
The end-stop is forced outward by the new factor cards.
15.50–18.00
A PRIME FACTOR IS MISSING.
Then:
THERE IS NO LAST PRIME.
Hold the general statement above the opened rack.
Include the compact general form:
N = p₁p₂…pₖ + 1.
N mod pᵢ = 1.
18.00–20.00
A fresh inspection plate slides over the mechanism.
Its engraved edge becomes the original end-stop.
Reset the hidden wheels.
Reveal the opening rack at the exact initial position.
REQUIRED MOTION
Every mechanical action must correspond to an operation in the proof.
Use linked rota

Write STORYBOARD.md with timed scenes covering the complete recording.

Then build the video. Make reasonable creative decisions and continue

Test a few representative frames and a short section before the full
render. Inspect the resulting images and frame sequences, fix visible
defects, and keep the animation practical for this computer.

Use efficient code-drawn textures if expensive watercolor effects
make rendering impractical.

DELIVERY
Render the complete video

author: ArchiveExplorer
title: Wireframe-First Ad
prompt: Write my launch video as 9 beats: pain, reframe, name, how it works, objection, range, mechanism in numbers, offer, CTA – one line each. For every beat write 3 headline options and send them to Jev to pick the one that best fits my brief. Build each beat as a wireframe first in HyperFrames: boxes, outlined text, guide lines, no color. Show me one still per beat and lock the timing. Then skin it from my DESIGN.md without moving the layout, and render a split view: final on the left, wireframe on the right.
postText:
jev + opus 5.5 is cracked at ad design...

motion designers won't like this video.

but nobody shows the part that makes an ad look expensive.

this video does. left: the finished ad. right: the same frames as a wireframe – boxes, guides, outlined text. synced start to finish.

AI copies structure way better than it imagines style. a wireframe is structure.

here's the skeleton this ad runs on. steal it for your product:

1. pain → "Streaks break."
2. reframe → "Momentum doesn't."
3. name → tideline + one line of what it is
4. how it works → the real UI, one action
5. objection → "Missed a day? Come back." "Not a reset."
6. range → "Any habit. Any pace."
7. mechanism in numbers → 10-day half-life, 8% floor
8. offer → "Pro free for 7 days"
9. CTA → "Every comeback counts. Start free"

how to build it wireframe-first:

1. write the 9 beats, one line each
→ if a beat needs two sentences, it's two beats

2. wireframe every beat
→ boxes for UI, outlined text, guide lines. no color, no photos
→ one still per beat. fix the layout before anything moves

3. lock the timing on the wireframe
→ cuts, holds and moves on the beat grid while changes are still cheap

4. let jev pick the words
→ write 3 headline options per beat, jev picks the one that fits your brief in milliseconds
→ you stop arguing with yourself over copy

5. skin it from DESIGN.md
→ colors, type and real components only now
→ the layout never moves, only the paint changes

6. render final | wireframe split
→ anything off on the right is off on the left too
→ that's your review pass

paste this into Claude Code 👇

"Write my launch video as 9 beats: pain, reframe, name, how it works, objection, range, mechanism in numbers, offer, CTA – one line each. For every beat write 3 headline options and send them to Jev to pick the one that best fits my brief. Build each beat as a wireframe first in HyperFrames: boxes, outlined text, guide lines, no color. Show me one still per beat and lock the timing. Then skin it from my DESIGN.md without moving the layout, and render a split view: final on the left, wireframe on the right."

the paint is the easy part. the skeleton is the ad.

author: shengtang135754
title: Opus 5.5 Remotion Product Promo Video
prompt:
You are a creative developer and motion graphics designer. Build a refined product video entirely through code using React and Remotion.

Treat this as a small motion graphics project. Think about the relationship between composition, typography, rhythm, and visual narrative versus implementation.

Project Details

Product Name: [Product Name]

Product Features: [Short Description]

Target Audience: [Audience]

Main Benefit: [One Clear Benefit]
postText:
你是一位创意开发者和动态图形设计师。完全通过代码使用 React 和 Remotion 构建一段精致的产品视频。

将此视为一个小型的动态图形项目。思考构图、排版、节奏和视觉叙述与实现之间的关系。

项目详情

产品名称：[产品名称]

产品功能：[简短描述]

目标受众：[受众]

主要优点：[一个明显的好处]

要突出显示的功能：[2–3 个功能]

可用资产：[屏幕截图、徽标、图标、品牌颜色]

结尾信息：[行动号召或标语]

时长：大约 15–25 秒

宽高比：[16:9 或 9:16]

创意方向

创建一个干净、现代的产品展示，具有清晰的视觉识别。产品应为主要焦点，辅以简明的文案和有目的的动画。

使用拘谨的色彩搭配、可读的排版、慷慨的留白和简单的背景。通过微妙的阴影、分层和缩放变化引入深度。

手机或浏览器的模型可以作为中心视觉元素。仔细构图并在场景间变化：全产品视图、对有用细节的特写，以及配有支持文本的更宽构图。

保持视觉语言的一致性。过渡、文本处理、颜色和设备展示应如同同一作品的部分。

故事与结构

在编写动画之前，建议做一个简短的分镜头剧本。对于每个场景，描述：

- 观众看到什么。

- 观众应该理解什么。

- 屏幕上的文案。

- 大致时长。

- 如何与下一个场景连接。

使用这个通用叙事作为起点：

1.⁠吸引

以简短的陈述开场，介绍好处或问题。让第一个构图立即易于理解。

2. 产品介绍

以清晰的设备或浏览器展示产品。明确它是什么，而不让观众感到信息超载。

3. 功能时刻

展示产品的两到三个实用方面。给予每个方面独立的时刻，并与具体的用户利益相连接。

4. 结尾

以简单的产品声明、徽标或行动号召结束。让最后一帧停留足够长的时间以便阅读。

根据提供的内容调整此结构。避免只是为了填充时长而添加场景。

产品展示

尽可能使用提供的屏幕截图和视觉资产。保持它们的比例，并确保重要的界面内容可读。

展示某个功能时，通过构图、特写或简洁的高亮引导注意力到界面的相关部分。

在资产缺失时，可以使用简化的界面元素。保持它们视觉上可信，并与产品描述清晰关联。不要虚构功能、客户声明或性能指标。

避免在每一帧中填满小的用户界面细节。精心挑选的界面部分往往比整屏幕更加清楚地传达信息。

运动方向

使用运动介绍信息、建立层次结构并连接场景。

思考性地结合几种简单技术：

- 平滑的进场和退场。

- 轻柔的位置和缩放变化。

- 具有清晰阅读顺序的文本暴露。

- 带有视觉元素过渡到下一个场景。

- 偶尔特写重要的产品细节。

变化节奏。有些时刻可以快速移动，而其他时刻应暂停，以便观众能够吸收信息。

保持相关元素的协调。如果文本介绍一个功能，相应的产品视觉应在自然时刻出现。

避免持续的运动、过度旋转和与内容相竞争的效果。让重要的构图停留。

排版与文案

撰写简短、具体的文案。优先选择清晰的好处而非模糊的营销声明。

在标题、支持性文本和小标签之间使用强大的层次结构。保持舒适的边距，仔细检查换行。

限制观众一次需要阅读的内容。如果一个句子需要长时间停顿，缩短它或将想法分跨场景。

根据预期的播放格式选择字体大小，包括在小屏幕上的回放。

实现

将视频组织成可重用的 React 组件和独立的场景。保持场景时长易于调整。

在实际操作中尽可能将可编辑内容（如文案、颜色和资产引用）与主要展示逻辑分开。

先构建总体序列，再精细调整各个时刻。确保视频以完整故事的形式运作，避免在装饰细节上花费太多时间。

使用简洁的方法，方便预览、修订和渲染。根据创意方向选择你自己的实现细节。

审核与完善

预览完整视频并检查代表性帧。

检查是否：

- 开场迅速传达。

- 每个场景都有一个明确的焦点。

- 文本可读，并在屏幕上停留的时间足够。

- 产品视觉清晰且比例正确。

- 过渡感到连贯。

- 没有所剪辑或意外重叠的内容。

- 结束部分显得有意图。

完善任何感觉匆忙、空洞、重复或视觉拥挤的场景。特别注意文本与产品图像之间的平衡。

交付物

提供：

- 一份简短的分镜头剧本。

- 正在进行的 React/Remotion 项目。

- 渲染的 MP4 文件。

- 一份简短的说明，解释如何更改文案、资产、颜色和时长。

如果缺少某些项目细节，请做出合理的创意假设，并简要说明。

使用参考作为质量和氛围的指导。发展你自己的构图和动画选择，而不是完全复制参考。

author: Cryptoxorz
title: Opus 5.5 Educational Explainer Video
prompt:
Help me make a science explainer video. Topic: {Topic} (Supplementary materials: {Paper/Link/Screenshot, Optional}; Target audience: {Zero-basis public / Some basis, Optional})

- Content: Explain one core question clearly, with a curiosity hook, counter-intuitive points, and life-like analogies, but facts must be accurate and sourced.
  - Prioritize citing original papers, authoritative institutions, and textbooks; do not use secondary marketing accounts.
postText:
帮我做一条科普视频，话题：{话题}（补充素材：{论文/链接/截图，可选}；目标观众：{零基础大众 / 有一定基础，可选}）

- 内容：讲清楚一个核心问题，有好奇心钩子、有反直觉的点、有生活化的类比，但事实必须准确、有来源。
  - 优先引用原始论文、权威机构和教科书，不用营销号二手说法。
  - 区分"已有共识""尚有争议""个人推测"，不夸大结论。
  - 开头 3 秒抛出最反常识的问题或现象，中间按"现象 → 原理 → 证据 → 意义"层层推进，结尾总结一句话结论，并抛一个开放问题引导评论。
  - 专业术语第一次出现时用一句大白话解释。
- 素材：从 NASA、Wikimedia Commons、YouTube 科普频道、B 站、论文配图、机构官网、新闻等广泛搜集，需要我协助就说。
  - 以视频片段为主（实验实拍、显微/天文影像、纪录片镜头），每句文案配合适的画面。
  - 抽象原理找不到实拍时，用代码生成示意动画或图解，不硬凑无关画面。
  - 图片和截图只偶尔点缀。不重复使用同一画面。裁掉原视频的字幕和台标。
  - 优先用公有领域 / CC 授权素材，标注来源。（可以借助 yt-dlp 下载素材）
- 规格：
  - 9:16 竖版，4–6 分钟，中、英两个版本。
  - Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS 配音，旁白清晰、语速适中。BGM 随旁白自动压低。
  - 全程右上角水印 Snail。
- 画面：
  - 第一帧做封面：最有冲击力的主体画面 + 大字标题（提问式或反常识式），越醒目越好。
  - 引用论文或数据时叠加原文卡片：英文原文高亮关键句，附中文翻译，注明期刊、年份、作者。
  - 关键数字、公式、对比用大字或简洁图表单独呈现，一屏只讲一个信息点。
  - 字幕每条说完一整句，可以 2–3 行，不截断单词。
- 交付前：
  - 逐条核对文案里的事实、数字、单位和引用出处，列出来源清单。
  - 用 STT 回听旁白（重点检查术语、人名、数字的读音），抽帧检查，检查重复镜头，确认画面与旁白内容对应。
  - 然后发我成片、720p 预览、封面和来源清单。

author: ivanainai
title: Interactive Stained-Glass Hibiscus Art
prompt:
Create a beautiful, interactive 3D browser artwork of a single stained-glass hibiscus flower.
Use the attached leaf as a reference for material delicacy, intricate veins, translucent colours and restrained presentation. Create an original flower composition.
postText:
Effort extra; prompt:
Create a beautiful, interactive 3D browser artwork of a single stained-glass hibiscus flower.
Use the attached leaf as a reference for material delicacy, intricate veins, translucent colours and restrained presentation. Create an original flower composition.
The flower is the entire experience. It fills most of the viewport against a quiet, near-black charcoal background.
FLOWER
Create five broad, organically shaped petals with gently ruffled edges, subtle asymmetry and graceful curvature. Arrange them into a convincing three-dimensional hibiscus, with natural overlap and a clearly visible centre.
Each petal is made from thin, luminous stained glass. Blend ruby pink, coral, pale peach and honey amber within the glass, with delicate marbling and fine branching veins radiating from its base.
Use extremely thin antique-gold seams and a finely beveled outer edge. Preserve the delicacy of the glass. Include a slender projecting central column with tiny golden anthers, a gracefully curved stem and two small translucent green leaves.
MATERIAL AND LIGHT
The glass must have visible thickness, coloured light transmission, subtle surface irregularities and crisp reflections that change with the viewing angle.
Overlapping petals should remain readable. Balance illumination so the colours stay luminous and the veins remain visible throughout rotation. Avoid large white reflections that erase the detail.
Use soft studio lighting with a warm backlight and a restrained rim light. Avoid excessive bloom, neon colour and heavy black outlines.
MOVEMENT AND INTERACTION
Start immediately with a flattering three-quarter view. Rotate slowly and smoothly so viewers can inspect the curved petals, thin edges and reverse side.
Allow dragging to orbit, scrolling to zoom, and a small pause control. Keep the flower fully framed during automatic rotation.
DELIVERY
Build actual 3D geometry rendered in the browser. Generate the geometry and textures in code.
Deliver a working preview and a downloadable, self-contained stained-glass-flower.html with all dependencies embedded.
Run the result, inspect a full rotation, and fix missing surfaces, transparency problems, clipping or washed-out lighting before finishing. Prioritize the quality of the flower over interface decoration.

author: theSethian
title: Show me the next 30 years. One shot, no cuts. Five stops: 2026, Earth at n…
prompt: Show me the next 30 years. One shot, no cuts. Five stops: 2026, Earth at night under a cloud of satellites; 2032, a ring around the planet with space elevators; 2040, a base on the Moon; 2048, cities on Mars; 2056, a swarm of mirrors circling the Sun. Continuous camera flight from Earth out to Mars, then back past Earth to the Sun. Every frame rendered by code from real planet maps.
postText:
I ASKED OPUS 5.5 TO SHOW ME THE NEXT 30 YEARS. ONE SHOT, NO CUTS.

For two days my feed has been full of Fable 5.5 films made from a single prompt. Anthropic hasn't announced that model, and people say some Fable 5.1 chats are getting routed to it.

The biggest one has 785K views. Someone asked Fable 5.5 to draw a simple dot and got back a little Pixar-style adventure.

So I gave the same kind of prompt to Opus 5.5, which Anthropic says performs at the level of Fable 5.1 on most work, and let it decide what comes next.

It came back with five stops:
- 2026, Earth at night under a cloud of satellites
- 2032, a ring around the planet with space elevators
- 2040, a base on the Moon
- 2048, cities on Mars
- 2056, a swarm of mirrors circling the Sun

The clip below is a continuous camera flight from Earth out to Mars, then back past Earth to the Sun. 

Every frame is rendered by code from real planet maps, with no video model involved. The music came later, a track I picked and had Claude lay under the visuals.

And that's the Opus you already have, before Fable 5.5 even ships.

author: twoclipping
title: Launch Trailer Video Generation
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: my product's name (one lowercase word), a 4-word tagline, the 3-step story of what it does, a launch date and domain, a royalty-free song with a clear drop, 4 vertical talking-to-camera clips and 12 portrait photos. If I skip any, use the defaults: "castr", "ugc ads, cast by ai", write a brief → scan 1,000 creators → cast 4, Mixkit "Cat Walk" (129.6 BPM, drop at 29.7s), free Pexels clips and portraits, and transparent stickers from Pixabay (serum, mic, megaphone, vintage camera, spotlight, lips).
</inputs>

<direction>
A 25 second square launch trailer, 1440x1440 at 60fps, loud poster style. Cobalt #2B3BFF, ink #0E0F1F, cream #F6E4C6, pink #FF7DC7, tangerine #FF5A1F. Archivo 900 extra-condensed for names, expanded for headlines, Geist and Geist Mono for labels. Op-art sunburst, scrolling waves, film grain. Real media only: the clips play inside the design, and the stickers get a white die-cut border and a soft shadow.
Motion rules: the camera never stops (a slow 1.03-1.07 push on every scene), nothing pops in (letters rise through a mask line one by one), nothing snaps to the beat (patterns rotate continuously), swaps are carousel glides of about 0.55s, colour changes fade over about 0.35s, stickers ease in and then keep a slow sway. No full stops after the wordmark or any headline.
Banned: beat-snapped rotations, pop-in slams, white flashes, crossfades between scenes, hard cuts, templates.
</direction>

<structure>
54 beats. The song starts 8 beats before its drop.
Beats 0-8: a cobalt sunburst turns around a breathing cream disc. The wordmark types in with a gliding caret and the tagline pill rises. The disc floods the frame into the drop.
Beat 8, the drop: the cream becomes the face of a 3D box and "ONE BRIEF" rises letter by letter. The camera pulls back to the box floating on waves. On beat 12 it turns to "1,000 CREATORS" (stacked, with outlined echoes), on beat 14 to "ZERO DMs".
Beats 16-22: a whip to a dark desk. A tangerine "BRIEF #042" ticket types its rows (product, vibe, cast, due), stickers drift on, a polaroid of a real clip drops onto the corner, and a "NOW CASTING" stamp presses down on beat 20.
Beats 22-34: the casting stage. A crowd of black and white portraits in an arc, a 3D stage block, and the creators gliding through like a carousel. Each plays live in a big disc in black and white, with their name in pink on the stage, their followers, and a MATCH % that counts up. One beat later a "CAST ✓" stamp lands and the clip fades to colour. A counter rolls 1/4 to 4/4.
Beats 34-39: pink floods out of the last disc. The disc morphs into a phone screen (the clip keeps playing) and fans into 4 phones playing all 4 creators, with views counting up. "4 ADS" and "BY FRIDAY" rise.
Beats 39-44, the music's break: the pink floor drops away and a cream "JOIN THE WAITLIST" ticket glides down onto the sunburst. On the pickup its stub tears off.
Beats 44-54: the ticket body morphs into a poster arch. The wordmark rises in, then the tagline, then an info bar slides up in 3 blocks (date, numbers, domain) and a ticker runs round the frame edge. Then it all folds back into the opening disc, so the last frame is the first.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. A beat map in beats, B = 60/BPM, with the song placed so its drop lands on beat 8.
3. The 3D box is an orthographic projection: each face is a 1440px offscreen canvas drawn with an affine transform and shaded by its normal.
4. Cut the clips to 30fps JPEG sequences with ffmpeg, draw frame floor(t*30), and do the black and white with ctx.filter.
5. Trim the sticker PNGs and add the die-cut border by dilating their alpha.

author: woojinrad
title: Colored-Pencil Explainer
prompt: Read the attached article and make a 25-second animated explainer (1080×1350, 24 fps) in a colored-pencil storybook style, drawn entirely in JavaScript on an HTML canvas, with a soundtrack synthesized using the Web Audio API. Pick 3 main ideas, give each a short caption taken from the text, and use one simple original character. Show me the storyboard first, then render it to MP4.
postText:
I don't know about you, but my feed is full of animations people are creating with @AnthropicAI's Claude Opus 5.5.

So I tried one with my 2024 Radiology editorial, "Seeing the Unseen." (https://pubs.rsna.org/doi/full/10.1148/radiol.240935)

Every colored-pencil stroke and every note of the music is code. No stock art. No image generator. It even replays my stress test from the paper. Change "absolute" washout to "relative," and the LLM's confident answer turns wrong.

Claude built the initial storyboard and draft, and I made a few tweaks. Claude handled the rest. Few tweaks, but seeing what's wrong still takes a human. Earlier this year, I created an entire product video using code (https://app.presto.run/), but this is the first time I feel like these frontier models can generate an animated explainer video that I'd be pretty happy with.

Try it yourself. Attach something you wrote or an article and paste this into Claude using Opus 5.5 (as of writing, I find Opus 5.5 does the best job at this):

"Read the attached article and make a 25-second animated explainer (1080×1350, 24 fps) in a colored-pencil storybook style, drawn entirely in JavaScript on an HTML canvas, with a soundtrack synthesized using the Web Audio API. Pick 3 main ideas, give each a short caption taken from the text, and use one simple original character. Show me the storyboard first, then render it to MP4."

title: Steam Engine Explanation
prompt: wie funktioniert eine dampfmaschine, gib mir das bitte als Erklärvideo im 3Blue1Brown-Stil aus
postText:
Ja, ich denke das ist ein großes Thema: Wir verbringen viel Zeit mit der Textausgabe der KI-Chat-Systeme. Das frisst einiges der eigentlich erreichten Zeiteffizienz der Arbeitsabnahme aus der Zusammenarbeit mit KI wieder auf bzw. erzeugt im Zweifel sogar mehr Zeit...
Aus der Lernpsychologie - Stichwort Picture-Superiority-Effekt (Bilder werden in Gedächtnisaufgaben oft besser erinnert als Wörter.) -wissen wir das kurze Sätze und erklärende Bilder das bessere Konzept sind, deshalb sind die hier empfohlenen Tipps genau richtig: 
- Texte in ASD-STE100 (oder etwa 80 % davon) erklären lassen.
- Lieber Diagramme oder interaktive HTML-Seiten erzeugen. "Gib mir das als HTML-Slideshow aus"
- Am besten maßgeschneiderte Erklärvideos, etwa im 3Blue1Brown-Stil.
Bei letzterem ist ja Claude mit dem Modell Opus 5.5 sehr gut. Der Prompt für das Video mit dem ich das einmal getestet habe lautete: "wie funktioniert eine dampfmaschine, gib mir das bitte als Erklärvideo im 3Blue1Brown-Stil aus"

author: qianqiongge
title: Remotion Product Demo
prompt:
请在当前项目做一支 15 秒的产品使用说明视频，使用 Remotion，竖版 1080×1920、30fps、共 450 帧。只用 assets 目录里提供的商品图和我给出的事实，不下载陌生素材，不补销售数据。

第 0 至 3 秒展示商品与一句使用场景。第 3 至 9 秒演示两步操作，每步只出现一个动作。第 9 至 13 秒展示结果，并保留能看清的停留时间。最后 2 秒显示产品名称，不加购买引导。

先列分镜与素材缺口，再做预览。字幕单独排版，动效以当前帧号计算。不要用真实时钟驱动时间线，也不要使用不固定的随机数。商品、文字、镜头时间分别配置，方便以后替换。

交付可编辑项目、启动与渲染命令、MP4，以及第 1、5、10、14 秒的静帧。缺少必要素材时停止并说明，不用假素材代替。”
postText:
Opus 5.5 做视频，怎么从动画代码走到 MP4？案例拆解＋可复制教程

歸藏用 Opus 5.5 做了一段抽卡动画。卡牌翻面、光效聚拢，最后把稀有卡放大，让观众看清结果。原视频约 18 秒，本文配的是带解读字幕的 12 秒节选，原作者 @op7418。

我核对了作者原帖、Anthropic 文档和两位创作者的制作记录。这篇讲制作方法，没有把别人的成片当成我的实测。

先弄清视频从哪里来

Opus 5.5 的官方能力是文字和图片输入、文字输出。它可以写动画程序，再由浏览器或渲染工具把画面导出。遇到真人口播、真实商品运动或复杂人物表演，通常还需要已有素材，或接入专门的图像、视频和配音工具。

歸藏在另一条原帖里提到，先得到 2D SVG 效果，随后要求改成更丰富的 3D 表现，并调整光效。这说明修改要求会直接影响成片。单看最终视频，无法知道经历了几轮对话，也不能证明其他人一次就能复现。

原始案例 https://x.com/op7418/status/2104085484347818226

这个案例有什么可以借鉴

画面先给期待，再逐张揭晓，最后让重点卡牌单独停留。三件事各占一段时间，观众不需要同时读十张卡。

做产品讲解时也可以借这种节奏。先展示一个具体问题，接着演示操作，最后停在结果上。需要替换的是主题和内容，不必照抄抽卡界面。

第一次做，先交付一支 15 秒短片

准备好你有权使用的图片、两三句经过核对的文案，以及参考画面。把它们放在独立项目目录。先做无配音版，避免把画面、声音和长篇脚本的故障混在一起。

在 Claude Code 中选择 Opus 5.5。使用 Anthropic 模型命名的环境，可以明确指定 `claude --model claude-opus-5-5`。第三方平台需要按自己的模型映射确认实际调用版本，不能只看界面标签。

下面这段是我整理的制作指令，尚未在 Opus 5.5 中执行，可作为第一轮需求。

“请在当前项目做一支 15 秒的产品使用说明视频，使用 Remotion，竖版 1080×1920、30fps、共 450 帧。只用 assets 目录里提供的商品图和我给出的事实，不下载陌生素材，不补销售数据。

第 0 至 3 秒展示商品与一句使用场景。第 3 至 9 秒演示两步操作，每步只出现一个动作。第 9 至 13 秒展示结果，并保留能看清的停留时间。最后 2 秒显示产品名称，不加购买引导。

先列分镜与素材缺口，再做预览。字幕单独排版，动效以当前帧号计算。不要用真实时钟驱动时间线，也不要使用不固定的随机数。商品、文字、镜头时间分别配置，方便以后替换。

交付可编辑项目、启动与渲染命令、MP4，以及第 1、5、10、14 秒的静帧。缺少必要素材时停止并说明，不用假素材代替。”

动画能播放以后，先检查四张静帧

看商品比例有没有变，字幕能否读完，画面最亮的时候有没有盖住主体。再连续播放检查转场，尤其是镜头切换时是否突然黑屏、丢字或重复动作。

返工可以这样说。

“只修改第 3 至 9 秒。两段字幕现在同时出现，改成顺序出现，每段完整停留至少 2 秒。保持其他场景、尺寸和商品图不变。重新导出这段预览，确认通过后再渲染全片。”

别停在网页预览

让 Agent 明确给出入口文件、Composition ID 和输出位置。假设项目入口为 `src/index.ts`，Composition ID 为 `ProductDemo`，可以在项目目录执行下面这条命令。

`npx remotion render src/index.ts ProductDemo out/product-demo.mp4 --codec=h264`

这些文件名必须和实际项目一致。Remotion 也支持从 JSON 文件读取 props，适合把商品名、字幕、素材路径放进配置，再批量渲染。Windows 环境优先用配置文件，避免内联 JSON 的引号被 shell 处理掉。

导出的 MP4 要重新播放。浏览器预览成功，仍可能在正式渲染时遇到字体未加载、外链素材失效或音轨不同步。

控制费用，从短片和复用开始

Anthropic 当前标准 API 价格是每百万输入 token 4 美元、输出 token 20 美元。订阅额度不能直接当成这张 API 价目表。

竹二木公开的个人测试里，一支 84 秒发布短片记为 2.96 美元；另一支音乐 MV 的第二轮累计 14.79 美元，包含中断续跑。这是他的记录，配音费也未全部计入，不能拿来承诺你的单条成本。

我的建议是先用 15 秒验证流程，保留跑通的项目。以后换商品、换字幕，尽量改配置和局部场景。科普、历史与模型对比视频还要先核事实，动画漂亮也可能把错误时间线讲得很顺。

这条路线更适合文字动效、图解、产品界面演示，以及需要反复修改的小片段。需要真实人物动作的镜头，继续交给拍摄素材或视频模型。把适合代码控制的部分留下来，才方便以后批量做。

title: Build "Jelly Dice": a single self-contained HTML file (all JS/CSS inline,…
prompt: Build "Jelly Dice": a single self-contained HTML file (all JS/CSS inline, no build step) with translucent gummy-candy dice that behave like real soft bodies. Render with raw WebGPU (WGSL shaders, no three.js). If WebGPU is unavailable, show a clean fallback card that
postText:
prompt:
Build "Jelly Dice": a single self-contained HTML file (all JS/CSS inline, no build step) with translucent gummy-candy dice that behave like real soft bodies. Render with raw WebGPU (WGSL shaders, no three.js). If WebGPU is unavailable, show a clean fallback card that explains why.

PHYSICS (the heart of it; it must feel like real jelly, not a rigid die with a wobble shader)
- Each die is a rounded cube simulated as a tetrahedral lattice with XPBD: co-rotational shape matching (per cell and per tet) for elasticity, tet volume constraints so it is nearly incompressible, and hard strain limits so it can never stretch without bound. Inverted elements must always recover.
- Floor contact with static and kinetic friction, plus a raised rim around the plate. Die–die contact against each other's rounded box, with friction.
- Separate rigid motion from deformation: rotational resistance on the floor, internal damping that only damps the wobble, never the rigid motion.
- Sleep when calm: settled dice must never jitter. Wake neighbours when an awake die comes close.
- Heavy landings soak up the rebound, so a dropped die squashes and settles instead of bouncing like rubber.

INTERACTION
- Drag a die to stretch it. The grab is compliant and progressive: a gentle pull stretches the jelly while its base clings to the plate, and a firm pull lifts and moves it. Cap the force, and allow no launches or wild spin on release.
- A quick tap pokes: a small squish into the surface, and the whole die rings.
- Drag the empty table to orbit the camera, pinch or scroll to zoom. The camera drifts gently toward where the dice are, never while one is held.
- Roll button (and Space / R): throw 1–5 dice (number picker). When everything settles, read each top face and show the values plus the total. A die resting cocked against another gets a small nudge (twice at most) before the result is read.

LOOK (photographic, like a product shot of real candy)
- Procedural photo studio: warm paper sweep, a big overhead softbox, a back-left strip light and a cool fill card.
- The dice sit on a frosted-glass plate with a bright rolled bevel, satin sheen and fine grain, casting its own soft shadow on the table.
- Candy material: real refraction (bend the ray in, find the exit depth from a back-face pass, look up what is behind), Beer–Lambert absorption by thickness so thin parts are light and the core is deep, thin edges glowing when the key light shines through, and glossy Fresnel skin with a crisp highlight.
- Pips: ivory dots set just under the skin in shallow concave dimples. Pips on the far faces stay visible through the body.
- Dice seen through other dice must refract correctly (depth layers wherever their screen footprints overlap).
- Soft shadows whose penumbra grows with distance; the shadows are tinted with the candy colour and lighter, because the candy is translucent. Contact occlusion from a top-down height map.
- Smooth normals from the deformation Jacobian (cofactor) on the GPU via a compute pass. Upload only node positions per frame.
- Six candy colours: Emerald, Amethyst, Amber, Sapphire, Raspberry, Lime. Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, MSAA, dither.

UI (editorial, minimal)
- Masthead top-left in Instrument Serif and Instrument Sans. Along the bottom: colour swatches, dice count, Roll button, total and the individual values.
- A settings panel with Softness and Wobble decay sliders, ¼ speed, Show mesh (lattice overlay), Sound (soft synthesised squelchy "tup" impacts, off by default), Pause, Reset dice and Reset view, plus an FPS readout.
- Responsive down to a phone (touch, pinch zoom), keyboard accessible, respects reduced motion.

Quality bar: the stretch, poke and landings should look and feel like real gummy candy at 60 fps. Test it headlessly with screenshots before handing it over.

author: imryven
title: Claude Code Multi-Agent Setup
prompt:
Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:

1. Look in ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents for subagents that already cover explorer, worker and researcher. Draft new ones only for roles that are missing. Set each to model: opus, effort: medium. If an existing subagent is pinned to a different model, list it, don't touch it.

2. Set the main session's effortLevel to high in ~/.claude/settings.json, and set advisorModel to fable.

3. Check for anything disabling the advisor: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, DISABLE_TELEMETRY, any variable blocking feature-flag fetches, and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, which overrides subagent effort. Report what you find. Change nothing yet.

4. Add one line to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before a large plan, when an error repeats, and before marking a long task done.

Show every change as a diff first. Don't touch anything until I say go.
postText:
Claude Code tip: if Opus 5.5 is already your main model, Fable 5.1 has been sitting idle this whole time.

wire it in with /advisor

start it with /advisor fable

Opus 5.5 writes every line. Fable 5.1 reads the whole session, every tool call, and says nothing until one of three moments:

→ a plan gets proposed: is this actually the right move, or just the first one?

→ the same error comes back twice: is the search stuck, or is this a dead end?

→ the task gets marked done: what got missed while it was moving fast?

Opus 5.5 ships. Fable 5.1 catches what would've shipped broken.

Jev engineering makes the same move one layer down: forks that don't need a real thinker, which file, which tool, retry or give up, get routed to Jev and answered in under half a second. the expensive model only ever sees the forks that genuinely split.

the tree this runs on:

> Opus 5.5, high effort, owns the main session

> explorer, medium effort, reads the code

> worker, medium effort, edits and runs tests

> researcher, medium effort, pulls the docs

> Fable 5.1 outside all of it, on call, never writing a line itself

author: Gdgtify
title: Kinetic Typography JFK Speech Film
prompt:
Create a 20.00-second kinetic typography film titled “ESCAPE THE ORBIT,” based on John F. Kennedy’s Rice University address, September 12, 1962.

The central experience: a sentence discovers that it can change its own trajectory.

Deliver one complete, self-contained HTML file. Composition: 1080×1080. Target: 60fps. Use Canvas, SVG, or embedded WebGL. Embed required assets and libraries. The film must work without audio.

EXACT DISPLAY TEXT
“We choose to go to the moon”
“[…]”
“not because they are easy,”
“but because they are hard”
Preserve this order. The bracketed ellipsis explicitly indicates omitted speech. Attribution is separate from the excerpt. No additional slogans.
ART DIRECTION
Background: midnight # 080D23.
Primary type: warm white # FFF4DD.
Trajectory: electric coral # FF654F.
Secondary orbital geometry: blue # 6685FF.
Use a broad, confident grotesque for the speech and a sharply drawn italic for the final emphatic word. Avoid the appearance of a spacecraft dashboard. No rockets, astronaut illustrations, starfield wallpaper, lens flares, or decorative telemetry.
The frame should resemble an exceptionally refined astronomical instrument that has become expressive.

CENTRAL VISUAL RULE
The baseline of the sentence is a trajectory.

At first it is trapped in a closed orbit. A rhetorical decision changes that orbit into an open path. The letters remain the same travelers throughout.
Use an abstract orbital metaphor; do not present invented mission data or imply a physically accurate flight simulation.
STORYBOARD
0.00–3.50
The opening excerpt appears across the center, large and horizontal. Reveal it in three meaningful phrase groups.
A single hairline ellipse passes behind the baseline. A small circular lunar mark occupies its distant focus.
Hold the completed phrase motionless for 700ms.

3.50–6.00
The camera pulls back. The previously straight baseline reveals a shallow curvature.

The phrase travels along the ellipse as a coherent unit. Keep its glyphs upright during the initial movement. Only after the reading hold may they progressively adopt the tangent of the path.

The viewer realizes the sentence is circling rather than advancing.
6.00–7.00
Show the bracketed omission in an uncluttered central opening. The orbital movement decelerates.

7.00–10.50
Reveal the next clause on the near side of the orbit. Its final word travels through one smooth, effortless arc and returns toward where it started.

This ease should feel elegant but unproductive. Avoid comic bouncing.

10.50–14.50
Reveal the final clause horizontally before transforming it.
At its emphasis, the ellipse opens at one precise point. The same tracked letter group takes the new tangent and departs.
Perform one deliberate 70-degree camera roll. Counter-rotate the active phrase so it remains readable while the orbital field changes orientation around it.

The trajectory sweeps from lower left to upper right. Acceleration is conveyed by expanding spacing between its trailing marks, not by shaking the camera.

14.50–17.00
The camera matches the departing phrase’s velocity. The phrase becomes visually still while the old orbit recedes beneath it.

The lunar mark enlarges into a restrained crescent through geometric overlap. The crescent brackets the destination without becoming a cartoon illustration.
17.00–20.00
Resolve into a spacious editorial composition containing the selected excerpt in reading order, including its omission marker.

The open trajectory runs through the margins and exits the frame. Hold the entire image completely still for the final 1.2 seconds.

CHOREOGRAPHY
Use only three camera operations: pullback, roll, velocity match.
Give each operation a rhetorical purpose.
